orgs.name: CARE AND SHARE INC
services: Regional food bank for Southern Colorado: distributes USDA TEFAP (The Emergency Food Assistance Program) food — fresh produce, dairy, meat and non-perishables — through partner food pantries across its service area (food box once a month with photo ID)
Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP) for seniors; Children's Nutrition Initiative sites; mobile food pantry events; a Find Food locator for partner pantries on its website
orgs.serves: low-income households across Southern Colorado (Colorado Springs distribution center, 2605 Preamble Point)

orgs.name: COMMUNITY HEALTH PARTNERSHIP
services: As Community Health Partnership (now ChangeLine), administered the Pikes Peak Continuum of Care (CO-504) from 2018 through June 30, 2026: CoC planning, HMIS data administration and Coordinated Entry for El Paso County
Its PPCoC data dashboard publishes HMIS / Built for Zero counts of homeless veterans and transition-age youth served in El Paso County
orgs.serves: system record — the Pikes Peak homeless-response system (providers and the public via Coordinated Entry), not walk-in direct services

orgs.name: GRECCIO HOUSING UNLIMITED INC
services: Affordable housing: 25+ owned/managed communities (apartments, townhomes, single-family homes), nearly 1,500 residents per year, including two senior (62+) communities
Eviction Prevention Program: financial resources for Greccio residents facing a one-time crisis (job loss, health issue) — RESIDENTS ONLY
Resident Resources: weekly no-cost food pantry and monthly senior Mobile Market (with Care and Share), financial literacy classes, scholarships, holiday programs
orgs.serves: low-income individuals and families (30-80% AMI) in El Paso and Teller Counties — services below are for Greccio residents

orgs.name: HOMEWARD PIKES PEAK
services: Housing First permanent supportive housing for chronically homeless individuals, families and veterans (HUD CoC grantee: $460,727 + $199,134 in FY2018 and $531,431 + $226,122 in FY2020 CoC awards)

Harbor House sober-living recovery home (transitioning to a family recovery home for parents with children in fall 2026); Project Detour sober living for women exiting incarceration; Bloom Recovery Home, a one-year structured sober living program for pregnant and parenting women
Outpatient substance-use clinical services (no sobriety required to enter treatment; pregnant and parenting women prioritized)
Street outreach with the Colorado Springs Police Department Homeless Outreach Team; The Commons, a 50-unit permanent supportive housing community (phase two planned)
NOTE: Homeward Pikes Peak's own FAQ states it does NOT offer direct emergency rental or mortgage assistance — it refers people in a housing financial emergency to 2-1-1
orgs.serves: individuals and families experiencing homelessness, substance use and mental health challenges in the Colorado Springs area

orgs.name: MT CARMEL VETERANS SERVICE CENTER
services: Military, Veteran & Family Services: financial coaching and assistance, housing and food aid, education programs, legal support, and homeless veteran outreach
Health & Wellness: onsite counseling, telehealth therapy, support groups, alternative therapies and retreats (open to veterans of all eras regardless of discharge status)

Transition & Employment: career transition assistance, employment workshops, MilSpouse Career Program and veteran job coaching; the Governor extended state funding five years for its Veterans Service to Career program
orgs.serves: military members, veterans and their families in Southern Colorado (headquarters 530 Communication Circle, Colorado Springs)

orgs.name: PARTNERS IN HOUSING INC A COLORADO NON-PROFIT CORPORATION
services: Family Self-Sufficiency Program: one year of transitional housing (68 units owned across Colorado Springs) with supportive services; families pay 30% of the previous month's income
Individualized caseworker, career readiness program, budget and credit counseling, life skills classes, housing navigation, healthcare access, childcare during program components
Two free donation centers for program families: furniture, clothing, baby items, food, hygiene products and household goods
orgs.serves: families with children experiencing homelessness or at imminent risk, in El Paso and Teller Counties

orgs.name: PIKES PEAK UNITED WAY
services: THE FRONT DOOR: Pikes Peak United Way operates 2-1-1 — call 2-1-1, text your ZIP to 898-211, or use 211colorado.org — for referrals to food, housing, utilities, emergency shelter, clothing, transportation, legal services, mental health, senior and veteran help; navigators responded to 34,000 people in 2024
Family Success Center and free VITA tax assistance at 518 N Nevada Ave, Colorado Springs
SYSTEM ROLE: selected by the Pikes Peak CoC Board (April 21, 2026) with the City of Colorado Springs as the CoC's next System Lead, effective July 1, 2026
orgs.serves: anyone in the Pikes Peak region looking for rent, utility, food, shelter or other help (2-1-1 serves a 12-county Southern Colorado area including El Paso County)

orgs.name: SILVER KEY SENIOR SERVICES
services: Reserve & Ride transportation: ADA-accessible rides to medical appointments, shopping, meal sites, senior centers, employment and VA medical facilities (call 719-884-2380 to schedule)
Nutrition: Meals on Wheels / home-delivered meals, Connections Café congregate meal sites, and a food pantry at 1625 S Murray Blvd (fresh, frozen and non-perishable items, including pet food)

Resource navigation, emergency assistance, companionship and activities at its campus; funded in part by Older Americans Act Title III via the Pikes Peak Area Agency on Aging, federal and state grants, and the City of Colorado Springs (per its own Connections Café guide)
orgs.serves: older adults (60+) in the greater Colorado Springs area

orgs.name: SPRINGS RESCUE MISSION
services: Emergency shelter: 450 beds, open every night of the year at 5 W Las Vegas St (the city's primary low-barrier shelter; up to 525 adult beds in the city's severe-weather protocol)
Samaritan's Kitchen: free breakfast, lunch and dinner daily
Resource Center: case management for housing, health and work goals; public showers (16) at the Resource Center
Work programs, job training and internship opportunities
orgs.serves: people experiencing homelessness and poverty in Colorado Springs and the Pikes Peak region

orgs.name: THE PLACE
services: Housing programs for youth: Permanent Supportive Housing (including The Launchpad, a 50-unit supportive housing community for ages 18-24 opened May 2025), Rapid Re-Housing (rent and utilities assistance with case management, typically 12 months or less), Rental & Utility Assistance, and Transitional Living
Street outreach and a Drop-In Center (showers, meals, laundry, case management)
Employment and education support (high school continuation, GED, college enrollment), health and mental health referrals, family reunification assistance
NOTE: the dedicated youth emergency shelter has permanently closed (City of Colorado Springs 2026 Annual Action Plan) — no Emergency Shelter tag is applied
orgs.serves: young people ages 15-24 experiencing homelessness or housing instability in the Pikes Peak region

orgs.name: TRI LAKES CARES
services: No-cost Market & Pantry: weekly shopping for fresh produce, dairy, meat and pantry staples once enrolled; one bag of emergency groceries with no enrollment
Housing Helping Hand: emergency rent or mortgage assistance and help with overdue utilities to prevent homelessness
Health Connection: help with prescription costs, doctor visit co-pays and insurance paperwork
Keep It Moving transportation help: bus passes, oil changes and minor car repairs
orgs.serves: individuals and families in northern El Paso County / the Tri-Lakes area (financial assistance limited to ZIPs 80132, 80133, 80921, 80840 and portions of 80908; food open to anyone)

orgs.name: WESTSIDE CARES INC
services: Rental assistance that kept 500 families housed in 2025, and utility support (408 households assisted with utility costs through LEAP / Project COPE in 2025)
Housing navigation (534 neighbors assisted in 2025; 50 previously homeless neighbors placed into permanent housing)

ID help: 875 IDs, birth certificates and school records provided in 2025; six food pantries / four-day food baskets and a hot meal; clothing, toiletries and laundry; nurse/doctor visits; transportation help from bus tickets to car repair; mail service for people experiencing homelessness
orgs.serves: neighbors in need on the west side of El Paso County (west of I-25), at 2808 W Colorado Ave, Colorado Springs
